brief: Q3 13F filings (Sept 30 snapshot) show hedge fund chip/AI positioning 36 days before the Nov 5 crash, when the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 12.25%. Tech long/short funds that were up 24% at the June peak, driven by momentum stocks up 125% through Q2, round-tripped to roughly flat YTD (-1%) as those stocks fell 56% since. Of four chip-heavy filers, three (Druckenmiller, Lone Pine, Situational Awareness) were already cutting exposure in Q3 while Tepper added, raising Micron and Nvidia and opening Applied Materials. Micron and Lam Research each fell about 17% five weeks later. Situational Awareness's 13F value fell 92% ($18.7bn) after a July margin-call-style unwind, then rebuilt as call options by September. Soros and Lone Pine built large Intel positions, a near-consensus long, while Nvidia sold about a quarter of its stake (about $6.5bn), more than it paid for the whole position. Goldman data show the US tech long/short ratio at a record low of 1.5, over 20 points underweight versus the S&P. The piece argues de-risking began before October, so the crash caught those who rotated or added, not those who had already cut.
